title: The Shs 2.4 trillion question Parliament cannot postpone
deck: A supplementary spending request has reopened an old argument about how Uganda counts its money — and who gets to see the books.

title: City Hall moves to reclaim the pavements. The traders are not moving.
deck: A week after enforcement teams cleared the walkways of Kikuubo, a fragile standoff has settled over the city's busiest trading streets.

title: Cabinet approves digital identity roadmap after two-year delay
deck: The plan would link national identification to mobile money, health records and school enrolment — raising questions about consent and cost.

title: Teachers suspend strike after pay talks breakthrough
deck: Unions say a phased salary adjustment will begin in January. Head teachers warn that term dates leave little room for recovery.

title: Flood warnings issued for eastern districts as river levels climb
deck: Emergency teams are pre-positioning supplies in six districts after a week of heavy rain upstream.

title: Cholera cases confirmed in three border towns
deck: Health teams have set up treatment units and are tracing contacts after cases were reported at crossings with two neighbours.

title: Court orders fresh audit of district road contracts
deck: Judges found that procurement records for 14 contracts were incomplete, and asked the auditor general to reopen the file.

title: Coffee exports hit a record. The farmer's share has not followed.
deck: A strong crop and firm prices have lifted earnings to an all-time high, but growers say the gains stop at the first buyer.

title: Mobile money agents push back on new float caps
deck: Agents say tighter limits will push customers back to cash. Regulators say the rules target a specific kind of risk.

title: Shilling steadies as the central bank mops up liquidity
deck: Traders describe a calmer week after a volatile October, with importers still cautious.

title: Ntinda tech hub opens with 200 desks and a waiting list
deck: The workspace is the largest of its kind outside the city centre, and its founders are betting on the suburbs.

title: Boda riders test electric bikes as fuel costs bite
deck: A pilot in three divisions offers battery swaps on credit. Riders are doing the maths on range and repayment.

title: Informal traders form a cooperative to buy wholesale
deck: Nine hundred vendors have pooled deposits to negotiate directly with suppliers, cutting out two layers of middlemen.

title: Cranes edge Zambia in a five-goal thriller under the lights
deck: A stoppage-time header settled a match that swung four times and left Namboole hoarse.

title: Kampala City go top after an 89th-minute winner
deck: A scrappy game turned on a substitution and a moment of impatience from the visitors' captain.

title: Nakato breaks the national 10,000m record in Nairobi
deck: The 23-year-old took eleven seconds off a mark that had stood for nine years, then apologised for not going faster.

title: Onyango signs with a Nairobi promoter and eyes a continental title
deck: The unbeaten welterweight says the move gives him the fights he could not get at home.

title: Sevens squad named for the Africa Cup with three uncapped players
deck: A youthful forward pack will face a difficult pool in Accra, where Uganda defend a title they won in 2024.

title: Women's league expands to 14 clubs — and finally gets a title sponsor
deck: The competition will play a full double round for the first time, with matches broadcast on radio.

title: The producer who turned boda horns into the song of the year
deck: A field recording of Kampala traffic became the most recognisable hook of 2026. Its maker is still riding to the studio.

title: Kampala film festival returns with 40 screens and a local-first lineup
deck: The programme is dominated by East African work, including six features making their debut in the city they were shot in.

title: Luganda pop is going global. The business is staying local.
deck: Streaming has taken the sound abroad. The money, the rights and the management are still being worked out at home.

title: The week Kololo ran on colour: fashion in 24 frames
deck: Backstage, on the runway and in the queue — the looks that defined the season's biggest showcase.

title: Twenty years of the late-night voice that kept Kampala awake
deck: From 10pm dedications to a podcast empire, the city's most enduring broadcaster on what changed and what did not.

title: Streaming platforms commission their first Luganda-language series
deck: Two productions will shoot in Kampala next year, with local crews and a share of the rights retained by the producers.

title: Our newsrooms must learn to listen
deck: We are excellent at broadcasting and less good at hearing. That is a business problem as much as a democratic one.

title: The budget is not the problem. The plumbing is.
deck: Every year we debate the number and ignore the pipes that decide whether it reaches a classroom.

title: A city that works for the people who sell on its pavements
deck: Kampala does not have a street trading problem. It has a market design problem.

title: Sport is Uganda's cheapest diplomacy
deck: One good tournament does more for the country's reputation than a year of consultants.

title: What the coffee boom should teach us about patience
deck: Value is not created at the auction. It is created by the person who waits, and we have been slow to reward her.
